source_text: Τίς οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν γενναῖος, τίς εὔσπλαγχνος, τίς πεπληροφορημένος ἀγάπης; εἰπάτω: Εἰ δἰ ἐμὲ στάσις καὶ ἔρις καὶ σχίσματα, ἐκχωρῶ, ἄπειμι, οὗ ἐὰν βούλησθε, καὶ ποιῶ τὰ προστασσόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ πλήθους: μόνον τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰρηνευέτω μετὰ τῶν καθεσταμένων πρεσβυτέρων. τοῦτο ὁ ποιήσας ἑαυτῷ μέγα κλέος ἐν Χριστῷ περιποιήσεται, καὶ πᾶς τόπος δέξεται αὐτόν, τοῦ γὰρ κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. ταῦτα οἱ πολιτευόμενοι τὴν ἀμεταμέλητον πολιτείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐποίησαν καὶ ποιήσουσιν.
pass_a_gloss: Who then among you is noble, who is kind-hearted, who is fully assured of love? let him say: If on account of me there is strife and quarrel and divisions, I withdraw, I depart, wherever you wish, and I do the things commanded by the majority: only let the flock of Christ be at peace with the presbyters appointed. He who does this will acquire great glory for himself in Christ, and every place will receive him, for the earth and its fullness belong to the Lord. These things those who live as citizens of the unregretted citizenship of God did and will do.

bible_refs.note: the earth and its fullness belong to the Lord

pass_b_english: Who among you is noble? Who is kind-hearted? Who is fully assured in love? Let that person speak up: 'If my presence has caused strife, quarreling, and division, I will step aside and leave. I will go wherever you wish, and I will do whatever the majority decides. Only let Christ's flock live at peace with the appointed presbyters.' The one who does this will win great glory for himself in Christ, and every place will welcome him, for the earth and all it contains belong to the Lord (Psalm 24:1). This is what those who live as citizens of God's unregretted citizenship have done and will continue to do.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass B correctly identifies the allusion to Psalm 24:1 (τοῦ γὰρ κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς) which was present in the Greek but lacked an inline citation in the source text; per instructions, adding the identification is required and correct. Pass A and B maintain the agency and nuances of the Greek.
